links.outcome: Confidence calibration of LLM outputs on bone tumor radiographs
links.effect: All models showed confidence miscalibration, with higher confidence in incorrect predictions and tumor-negative cases; systematic overconfidence especially in GPT-4.1.
links.quote: All models demonstrated confidence miscalibration, with higher confidence observed in incorrect predictions and in tumor-negative cases.

links.outcome: False negative and false positive rates of LLM radiograph interpretation
links.effect: False negative rates: GPT-4.1 29.9%, ChatGPT 24.8%, Gemini 6.6%. False positive abnormality rates: GPT-4.1 40.7%, Gemini 25.9%, ChatGPT 13.5%.
links.quote: False negative rates varied substantially, with GPT-4.1 demonstrating the highest rate (29.9%), followed by ChatGPT (24.8%) and Gemini (6.6%).

screen.reason: The study benchmarks the diagnostic accuracy, false negative/positive rates, hallucination rates, and confidence calibration of multimodal LLMs on a retrospective radiograph dataset, without evaluating a specific deployment safeguard or practice.
